From a Mongolic language. Compare Mongolian хуралдай (xuraldaj).
Borrowed from Mongolic; compare Kalmyk мөрн (mörn, “horse”).

parole.significato: saxaul (any of three species of the amaranth genus Haloxylon)
parole.testo: Ultiamately Mongolic, compare Mongolian заг (zag), Kalmyk за (za).

parole.significato: thousands, a multitude, a host, lots of
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic тьма (tĭma), borrowed from a Mongolic language, from Proto-Turkic *tümen.
From a Mongolic source, compare Mongolian хаан (xaan), ultimately from the same Turkic source as кага́н (kagán). A possible intermediary is Chagatai خان (xan).

parole.significato: zokor (any of several Asiatic burrowing rodents native to Central Asia)
parole.testo: A Mongolic borrowing, ultimately from Proto-Mongolic *sokar (“blind”) (whence Mongolian сохор (soxor)), which is often used with Proto-Mongolic *noman (“mole; vole; zokor”).
